draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Panchgani! The British laid out this hill station in the 1860s on a nameless patch between five villages, which is where the name comes from. Just up the road is Table Land, a 4,500 ft plateau said to be the second largest in Asia.
draft.hungryLine: You can't leave without a strawberry cream, fresh cream and strawberry slices with a scoop of strawberry ice cream on top, sold everywhere from fancy restaurants to roadside stalls.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Table Land is about a 10 min walk, with horse rides, snack stalls and huge views. Sydney Point looks out over Dhom Lake and the Krishna valley.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Grab a bench at Sydney Point, some of them are solar powered so you can even charge your phone while you watch the paragliders.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Freddie Mercury went to school here, at St. Peter's School, which opened in 1904 as the European Boys' School.

spots.name: Table Land
spots.detail: 10 min walk · A huge 4,500 ft plateau with sunrise and sunset views, horse rides and snacks

spots.name: Sydney Point
spots.detail: In Panchgani · Views of Dhom Lake, the Krishna valley and Kamalgad Fort, plus a hanging bridge

spots.name: Parsi Point
spots.detail: In Panchgani · Once a Parsi meeting spot, now a viewpoint over the cliffs and Dhom lake with food stalls

legends.title: The Pandavas' kitchen
legends.body: Just south of Table Land is a spot locals call Devil's Kitchen. It's believed the Pandavas cooked here during their exile.

tips.title: Come in the monsoon for waterfalls.
tips.body: The area's many waterfalls only flow during the monsoon.

tips.title: Pick your horse ride at Table Land.
tips.body: There are short rounds, big rounds and multi-point rounds, plus a horse carriage that takes four people.

story.title: Land between five villages
story.body: Lord John Chesson surveyed these hills with Rustomji Dubash and chose a nameless area around Dandeghar, Godavali, Ambral, Khingar and Taighat. It was named Panchgani, and Chesson became its superintendent.

story.title: A town takes shape
story.body: Chesson invited tailors, dhobis, butchers, vegetable sellers and builders to settle below the bazaar, an area now called the gaothan. He's also credited with planting western trees like silver oak.

story.title: Boarding school town
story.body: St. Peter's School opened as the European Boys' School on a 58 acre hill campus. Panchgani is still known for its many boarding schools.

story.title: Strawberries and viewpoints
story.body: Panchgani and Mahabaleshwar are twin hill stations, and strawberries grow all over the region. Visitors come all year for the cliffs, lakes and viewpoints.
